what: the card-state evidence behind E72's handoff claims, with what is committed and what is not
written: 2026-10-27 (Tue, week 44) at the desk, as a correction: the first write-up cited a kernel-log pair and a 15:24:48 read-back as 'kept with the data', and neither was ever committed.

committed_in_this_directory.return_burst_telemetry: aifoundry2/e72back-smoke/p901 - 114 samples at 600, 2 at 700, 98 at 800 MHz

independent_ettelem_config.status: the raw output was printed to the session and not saved; the committed back_check 17 s earlier carries the same five fields, and two later independent reads below agree

module_uptime.means: the service processor had not reset since the host booted, so the restored 65 W is a real write and not a reboot default

kernel_log_error_event_counts.status: counted on the host at the time and reported; the dmesg output itself was not saved

independent_reads_afterwards.by: the verifier, one read-only ettelem config under the card lock (flock -w 5, timeout 10), et-who empty before and after
independent_reads_afterwards.kernel_log: Error Event Detected count 234; last one at host uptime 84342 s (about 14:38 PDT, before E72's window)

independent_reads_afterwards.by: the desk correction pass, read-only on the host only - no device node opened, no card lock taken, no card touched (another experiment held the card at the time)
independent_reads_afterwards.means: the count has not moved since before E72 started, so E72 added none; of the three 'Mgmt: Tried to open same device multiple times' lines only the one at host uptime 85783.9 s (about 15:02:27 PDT) is inside E72's window, and E72 recorded it as self-inflicted

firmware_at_handoff.status: re-read after the last run and reported; unchanged by construction - no flash, PMIC, reset, driver, PCIe, clock or voltage action was performed

lesson: a gate's evidence is only as good as the file it lands in: print-and-report is not committed evidence. The governor harness should write every end-of-session read into gov.jsonl, as it does for the sets.
